title: The task form always sends category 'coordination', so the new 'chosen category wins' rule switches off title-based area matching for every task made or edited in the app
evidence: TaskDelegationService::inferArea (and the same four lines in ai-service/app/engines/task_delegation.py infer_task_area): `$chosen = strtolower(trim((string) $type)); if (isset(self::POSITION_RELEVANCE_MAP[$chosen])) { return $chosen; }`. The client never sends an empty category: TasksPage.jsx:120 `category: 'coordination'` (form default), :540 the select offers only `['coordination', 'finance', 'publicity', 'documentation', 'logistics']` with no blank option, :367 `previewTaskRecommendation({ title: form.title, task_type: 'regular', category: form.category, ... })`, :268 `category: form.category`, :298 `category: task.category || 'coordination'` and :322 `category: editForm.category` on every edit. Verified with tinker on today's tree: inferArea('Prepare the budget liquidation report', 'coordination') returns 'coordination'; with null it returns 'finance'. Before today the category was only appended to the title haystack, so 'budget' matched finance first.
impact: An Admin who types 'Prepare the budget liquidation report' and leaves the category select on its default now gets the task scored as coordination: President and Vice Presidents are the primary match (100) and the Treasurer and Auditor drop to unrelated (40), in both the Python engine and the PHP fallback. The position factor is the heaviest part of the formula, so the recommended officer is wrong for most finance, publicity, documentation and logistics tasks unless the Admin remembers to change a field labelled optional. The edit form also writes 'coordination' onto tasks whose category was null (including event workflow tasks) on any save, so a later reassignment of those tasks is ranked as coordination too. No test covers it: TasksAiAuditFixesTest and test_engines.py only check a deliberately chosen category and a missing one, never the value the client really sends.
fix: Make 'no category chosen' a real state. In TasksPage.jsx give both category selects a first option `<option value="">Decide from the title</option>`, default the create form to `category: ''`, load the edit form with `task.category || ''`, and send `category: form.category || null` (create, preview and edit). Keep inferArea as written, so only an explicitly chosen area overrides the title. Show 'Decided from the title' in the task detail when category is null instead of `capitalize(selectedTask.category || 'coordination')`. Add a server test that POST /api/tasks/recommendation with title 'Prepare the budget' and no category yields task_area finance and with category 'logistics' yields logistics, and a client test that the default preview payload carries no category.

title: Officer eligibility now compares position titles byte for byte in PHP, so an officer whose title differs from the positions list only in case, spacing or dash type is dropped as 'inactive position'
evidence: New eligibleOfficers(): `&& in_array($officer->position_title, $activePositions, true)`; officerPayload() :775 `'policy_eligible' => in_array($officer->position_title, $this->activePositions($request), true)`; TaskDelegationService::recommend :89 `! in_array($officer->position_title, $activePositions, true) => 'inactive_position'`. The removed eligibleOfficerQuery() did this in SQL: `->whereColumn('sbo_positions.title', 'users.position_title')`, which on the production MySQL collation ignores case and trailing spaces. Titles are not stored canonically: UserController.php:1202-1215 validates with `->where('title', $positionTitle)` (case-insensitive on MySQL) and then stores what was typed (`$data['position_title'] = $positionTitle`), and an election hand over stores the election position's own title (OfficerAppointmentService.php:98/112, seats matched only through `SboPosition::normaliseTitle`). User::officerCanBookVenues already falls back to the normalised title for this reason ('so "Business-Manager" meets the "Business Manager" row').
impact: On production an officer saved as 'secretary' or 'Vice President - Internal' (hyphen) against a list holding 'Secretary' or 'Vice President – Internal' (en dash) was assignable yesterday when only case or trailing space differed, and is rejected today with 'Tasks can only be assigned to active SBO Officers with an assigned position.' The officers this fix was written for, those seated by an election, carry the ballot's title and so are the likeliest to be left out of the pool, the recommendation and the event plan. The local tests cannot see it because SQLite compares case-sensitively either way.
fix: Add one helper to TaskDelegationService, e.g. `canonicalPosition(?string $title, array $activeTitles): ?string`, that returns the active sbo_positions title whose `SboPosition::normaliseTitle()` equals the officer's (exact match first), or null. Use it in eligibleOfficers(), officerPayload() (policy_eligible, and send the canonical title as position_title to the Python engine), ineligibleEvaluation(), the preferred_role filters at TaskController.php:703 and :814, and recommend() line 89, and pass the canonical title to roleScore()/localAssignmentScores so the tier lookup, which is also exact, scores the officer correctly in both engines. Add a test with a profile title 'vice president - internal' against the position 'Vice President – Internal'.

title: Removing a draft while it is being saved overwrites 'accepted' with 'discarded', which disarms the new 'already has a saved to-do list' guard and lets a second task set be created
evidence: discardWorkflow checks the route-bound copy `if ($aiOutput->decision_status !== 'pending') { return ... 409 }` and then writes unconditionally: `$aiOutput->update(['decision_status' => 'discarded', ...])`. Today's confirm takes `AiOutput::whereKey($aiOutput->id)->lockForUpdate()->first()` (line 948) and its duplicate guard reads `->where('decision_status', 'accepted')->exists()` (lines 952-955).
impact: Two Admins (or two tabs) on the same draft: one presses Save and assign tasks, the other presses Remove while the confirm transaction is still inserting. The discard read 'pending' before the lock, waits on the row, then sets 'discarded' after the confirm commits. The tasks and notifications exist, the draft reads 'Removed', and because no draft is 'accepted' any more a later draft for the same event confirms and creates the whole task set again, which is the duplicate the lock was added to stop.
fix: Make the discard conditional and atomic: `$changed = AiOutput::whereKey($aiOutput->id)->where('decision_status', 'pending')->update([...]); if ($changed === 0) return 409 'This draft has already been saved or removed.'` Add a test that discarding an accepted draft through a stale model instance returns 409 and leaves it accepted.

title: Confirming two different drafts of one event at the same moment deadlocks on MySQL and one Admin gets a 500 instead of the 409
evidence: Each confirm locks only its own draft, `$current = AiOutput::whereKey($aiOutput->id)->lockForUpdate()->first();`, checks for an accepted draft with a plain read, and near the end updates the other drafts: `AiOutput::where(...)->where('reference_id', $event->id)->whereKeyNot($aiOutput->id)->where('decision_status', 'pending')->update(['decision_status' => 'discarded', ...])` (line 1063). `DB::transaction(function ...)` is called with the default single attempt.
impact: Confirm of draft 1 holds row 1 and needs row 2 for the bulk update; confirm of draft 2 holds row 2 and needs row 1. InnoDB picks a victim, Laravel rethrows the deadlock, and that Admin sees the generic 'Something went wrong' instead of 'This event already has a saved to-do list.' No duplicate tasks result, so this is only a wrong error on a rare race. 'confirming twice creates one task set' runs the two confirms one after the other on SQLite, so neither the lock nor this path is exercised by a test.
fix: Serialise on the event instead of the draft: as the first statement of the transaction run `Event::whereKey($event->id)->lockForUpdate()->first()` (the pattern already used at EventController.php:608), then re-read the draft's decision_status and run the accepted check. Every confirm for the event then queues and the second one reaches the existing 409.

title: The edit form's new date-and-time deadline is sent as browser-local wall time and read by the server as Manila time
evidence: `...(editForm.deadline !== isoToLocalDateTimeInput(editingTask.deadline) ? { deadline: editForm.deadline } : {})` with `<Input type="datetime-local" ...>` at line 1015. isoToLocalDateTimeInput (utils/dateTime.js) builds the value from `date.getFullYear()`, `getHours()` and so on, which is the browser's zone, and the string goes out with no offset. The server reads it with `Carbon::parse($data['deadline'])` in the app zone (config/app.php: Asia/Manila) in update() and changedDeadlineError(). The events screens avoid this by sending `localDateTimeToIso(...)` and reading it with `$this->localTime(...)`.
impact: On a device whose clock is not set to Philippine time (a laptop left on UTC, an officer abroad) the form shows a 5:00 PM Manila deadline as 9:00 AM, and changing it to 10:00 AM stores 10:00 AM Manila, seven hours earlier than intended. For an event workflow task the phase check then runs on the shifted time, so a valid 'during the event' time can be refused or an invalid one accepted. Before today the field was a date, so the shift could not happen.
fix: Send `deadline: localDateTimeToIso(editForm.deadline)` from handleEditSubmit, and in TaskController::update convert before use: after normalizeDeadline, when the value is not a bare date set `$data['deadline'] = $this->localTime($data['deadline'])->toDateTimeString()` and pass that Carbon to changedDeadlineError. Without the server half an ISO string ending in Z would be stored eight hours off, because the datetime cast formats without converting the zone. Add a server test that PUT with '2026-11-20T09:00:00.000Z' stores 17:00:00.

title: The standard-checklist notice tells the Admin their planning context was not used and 'is still above' even when none was typed or the draft was opened from history
evidence:
`{workflowMeta.template &&

This is a standard checklist built from the event dates, not a plan written for this event. The planning context you entered was not used and is still above, so you can change it and draft again.

}` is shown for every template draft, including those set by openWorkflowDraft() from 'Previous drafts' (line 977). The server overview for the rejected case likewise always says `The context you typed was not used.` (EventController.php:1463).
impact: An Admin who drafts with the context box empty, or reopens an old standard checklist days later, is told that text they entered was ignored and can be found above, where the box is empty or holds different text. It reads as lost input on a screen whose job is to be trusted before tasks are assigned.
fix: Render the second sentence only when it is true: in the client show 'The planning context you entered was not used and is still above...' only when `planForm.requirements.trim()` is non-empty and the draft came from the generate call in this session (keep a flag in workflowMeta, false in openWorkflowDraft). In templateWorkflow() add 'The context you typed was not used.' only when `trim($context['requirements']) !== ''`.
